headline: dYdX V4 is a Cosmos SDK L1 chain — no EVM addresses in address_book; Ethereum-side bridge contracts referenced but not fetched; 0 addresses confirmed this run

findings.text: D1: dYdX V4 runs on its own Cosmos SDK / CometBFT chain (chain-id dydx-mainnet-1); canonical block explorer is Mintscan (https://www.mintscan.io/dydx). EVM explorers (Etherscan, Basescan, etc.) do not host dYdX V4 chain state. Mintscan was not fetchable this run. No EVM name-tag search was possible.

D2: Official docs at https://docs.dydx.xyz and https://docs.dydx.exchange confirmed; no dedicated 'Deployed contracts' page found for the V4 chain. The docs contain node/validator infrastructure (seed nodes, RPC endpoints, upgrade history) but no on-chain module addresses in EVM format. The dYdX Foundation governance-contracts repo (https://github.com/dydxfoundation/governance-contracts) references an Ethereum-side deployed addresses page at https://docs.dydx.community/dydx-governance/resources/technical-overview — fetch was blocked.

D3: No audit_links provided in per-protocol context. The dydxfoundation/governance-contracts README references PeckShield audits for LiquidityStakingV1, StarkProxyV1, SafetyModuleV1, MerkleDistributorV1, and audits for WrappedEthereumDydxToken, GovernanceStrategyV2, and TreasuryBridge (audit reports in https://github.com/dydxfoundation/governance-contracts/tree/master/audits). Those are Ethereum V3-era contracts, not V4 chain-native. No V4-specific audit PDFs were surfaced.

D4: GitHub org https://github.com/dydxprotocol confirmed; key V4 repos include v4-chain (Go, the core protocol), v4-web (TypeScript frontend), v4-clients (TypeScript/Python/Rust), v4-documentation (MDX). Network genesis and validator config hosted at https://github.com/dydxopsdao/networks/tree/main/dydx-mainnet-1 (fetch blocked). No Foundry/hardhat deployment artifacts — Cosmos SDK chains do not use EVM deployment scripts.

D5: protocol.chains = ['dYdX'] — single chain only (dydx-mainnet-1). No multi-chain EVM enumeration required. Note: the DYDX governance token has an Ethereum presence (wethDYDX / bridge contracts) that is separate from V4 chain operations.
D6: No EVM factory contracts applicable. dYdX V4 perpetual markets are instantiated via on-chain governance proposals (x/gov module on the Cosmos chain), not EVM factory calls.

D7: Role taxonomy cannot be populated without fetched on-chain data. Cosmos governance (x/gov) module serves as the 'governor' actor; validators serve as block proposers/signers. No EVM multisig/timelock/proxy-admin addresses discovered.

D8: Zero addresses confirmed via fetched URLs this run. No admin_addresses[] entries can be made without violating anti-fabrication rules. The dydxfoundation/governance-contracts GitHub snippet references Ethereum-side contracts (WrappedEthereumDydxToken, TreasuryBridge, GovernanceStrategyV2) but their addresses were not present in the fetched snippets.

rationale.verdict: Assessment blocked at address-level resolution. dYdX V4 is a Cosmos SDK L1 with no EVM smart contract surface on the V4 chain itself. The Ethereum-side bridge/token contracts (wethDYDX, TreasuryBridge, GovernanceStrategyV2) exist but their addresses were not recoverable from fetched pages this run (https://docs.dydx.community and GitHub were fetch-blocked). Mintscan block explorer for the Cosmos chain was not fetched. The next run should inherit the docs.dydx.community governance address page and the dydxopsdao/networks genesis file as seed URLs to extract validator/governance Bech32 addresses.

protocol_metadata.about: dYdX V4 (dYdX Chain) is a standalone Layer 1 blockchain built on Cosmos SDK and CometBFT proof-of-stake consensus, purpose-built for perpetual futures trading. Users place leveraged long/short orders on crypto perpetual markets via a fully decentralized, off-chain orderbook and on-chain matching engine operated by validators. The protocol is governed by DYDX token stakers through on-chain governance proposals (Cosmos x/gov module), which control protocol upgrades, market listings, and fee parameters. Unlike prior dYdX versions (V1–V3), there are no EVM smart contracts on the V4 chain itself; the Ethereum-side components are limited to a wrapped DYDX token and bridge contract for cross-chain token migration.
